scope_note: Up to 20 publicly documented award records per funder. Public award pages are not application texts; null means unavailable, never absent. Detailed citations and evidence are in journalism.md.

funders.name: Fund for Investigative Journalism

criteria.claim: New, investigative exposure of wrongdoing; concrete question, preliminary findings, reporting roadmap, publication commitment and justified reporting-expense budget.

eligibility.claim: Freelancers, staff reporters and outlets; full investigations need a US outlet commitment; foreign work needs a strong US angle and US English outlet.

people.name: Bill Marimow; Ellen Weiss; Alan Berlow; Anu Narayanswamy; Diana Jean Schemo

communication_advice.advice: Pitch a concrete, outlet-committed investigation into a defined abuse of power; make the tool an essential reporting cost, not a standalone product.

funders.limitations: 2025 award announcement names recipients and tier but protects individual story details; 20-record sample is bounded, not exhaustive.

funders.name: Journalismfund Europe

criteria.claim: Expert-led review, added value, societal relevance, newsworthiness, original method/storytelling, feasibility, team, cross-border and EU-watchdog value.

eligibility.claim: European Cross-border teams need at least two professional journalists/outlets from two European countries and 80% EU-country budget.

communication_advice.advice: An eligible reporting team should connect the tool to a defined cross-border public-interest investigation, expert/security review and feasible publication plan.

funders.limitations: The selected official microgrants listing names 26 organizations but omits per-project title, leader and individual award amount. The detailed 20-name list is preserved in journalism.md.

funders.name: Investigative Journalism for Europe

criteria.claim: Cross-border relevance, public relevance, newsworthiness, research/publication plan, impact, feasibility, credentials, risk assessment and need.

eligibility.claim: Teams in at least two eligible European countries and publication in respected platforms in at least two eligible countries.

communication_advice.advice: Frame the tool as risk-assessed infrastructure for a named, eligible cross-border investigation and publication plan; IJ4EU also offers a secure OSS workspace after assessment.

funders.limitations: The April 2024 announcement has 17 awards but withholds many team names. Full list in journalism.md; selected data below preserves the most feature-relevant public entries.

funders.name: Pulitzer Center

criteria.claim: ML reporting: specific public-interest reporting project, transparent/verified methodology, outlet path, reproducibility/code-data plan, budget and work evidence.

eligibility.claim: General reporting grants serve journalists/newsrooms with specific story/series and outlet commitment; no broad concepts, basic equipment or startup seed money.

people.name: Lisa Gibbs; Marina Walker Guevara; Karol Ilagan; Joanna S. Kao
people.role: CEO; Executive Editor; Information & AI editors (current directory)

communication_advice.advice: Use a journalism-led investigation as the core, with pseudonymization as a verifiable reporting method and a safe reproducibility plan rather than a standalone product.

funders.limitations: Published examples do not consistently state individual award year/amount. Current staff roles are not historical selection evidence. Fifteen precedent names are in journalism.md.
